headline: Your eyes don't see—they collect light; your brain creates the image
universal_truth: What we perceive as reality is a construction, not a recording
fun_facts: Your eyes have about 130 million light-detecting cells, but only 1 million nerve fibers to carry signals
The image on your retina is upside down—your brain flips it right-side up
You have a blind spot in each eye where the optic nerve connects—your brain fills it in
discussion_questions: How does knowing your brain constructs vision change how you trust what you see?
What might you be 'filling in' without realizing it?
Why do you think illusions work so well on us?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: You think you see the world as it is. But here's the truth: your eyes collect light; your brain invents the picture. What you 'see' is a construction—filled with gaps, corrections, and assumptions you never notice. Vision is creative fiction.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Light enters your eye, hits your retina, and somehow becomes the vivid 3D world you experience. But the retinal image is flat, upside down, and has gaps. How does messy input become seamless experience?
cliff.prompt: How does the brain create vision?

options.text: The brain processes, flips, and fills in the raw signals to construct a coherent image
options.response: Yes. Your brain does enormous processing—correcting, interpreting, and constructing what you 'see.'

options.text: The eye captures a complete image that the brain simply displays
options.response: The eye captures light, but the brain's role is far more active...

q1.title: Upside Down World
q1.script: Like any lens, your eye projects an inverted image onto your retina—the world is literally upside down in your eye. Your brain automatically flips it. You've never noticed because it's been happening since birth.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Upside Down World"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: The Blind Spot
q2.script: Where your optic nerve exits the eye, there are no light receptors—a blind spot. You don't see it because your brain fills in the gap using surrounding information. You have blind spots right now, invisible because of invented data.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Compression Required
q3.script: Your retina has 130 million photoreceptors but only 1 million nerve fibers to the brain. That's 130-to-1 compression. Your eye does heavy processing before signals even leave—editing reality before your brain receives it.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Perception is construction, not recording. Vision reminds us that what we experience as 'reality' is our brain's best interpretation, not raw truth. Humility about our perceptions makes us wiser.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 84. Tomorrow, we'll explore how your ears work. Until then, remember: you're not seeing the world—you're seeing your brain's story about it.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Perception Humility - Question What You See
growTrack.activity: Find an optical illusion online. As you watch your perception shift, notice: you KNOW what's true, but you can't stop seeing the illusion. This is a reminder that perception isn't always reliable. Where else might your brain be constructing rather than recording?
